clauses.mechanism: own terms: fixed term of sixty days beginning to run on the date of this order, September 24, 1945 (recorded later reading)
clauses.reason: The sole clause amends paragraph 2 of EO 9611 to read "shall consist of the following members:" with a new list of three members, and provides: "The period of sixty days specified in" paragraph 1 of EO 9611 "begin to run on the date of this Order." (the words "paragraph 1  of the said Order, shall" lie between them). The signature date is "September 24, 1945." so the sixty days run from September 24, 1945. Counting September 24 as the first day, the sixtieth day is November 22, 1945; counting from the day after, the sixty days are complete on November 23, 1945. The recorded end is November 23, 1945 (the later reading). The new membership and the starting of the period operate only while the Board is re-established, so both end with the period. EO 9611 paragraph 1 also allows a shorter period for completion of the Board's functions; no held source dates an earlier completion. The first-end source is the held Federal Register text of the order. The commands of EO 9611 other than paragraph 2 and the period start are outside this clause.

research_rationale:
EO 9627 was read in full in the registered Federal Register text layer (jobs/fr-originals/data/full_run/texts/EO_9627.txt, 10 FR 12113, PDF page 1); the census register row (date, title, President) agrees with the heading, title and date line printed in that text. The order amends paragraph 2 of EO 9611 of September 10, 1945 (which re-established the Advisory Board on Just Compensation for sixty days) to name a new membership after Judge John J. Parker became unable to serve, and provides that the sixty-day period in paragraph 1 of EO 9611 begins to run on the date of this order. Page location was checked against the PDF page markers of the held text layer only; no page image was inspected. The representation is a machine-extracted text layer of the official PDF, held as original_representation_unverified. The period of the Board's re-establishment is fixed by EO 9611 paragraph 1 and restarted by this order; the end below follows from this order's own sentence about the period.

savings.reason: The order contains no savings or transfer clause. Its two commands (the new membership of the Board and the start of the sixty-day period) have no residual effect once the Board's period ended, and the machine searches of the U.S. Code and the eCFR and the Federal Register catalog return no hit citing EO 9627. Whether the direction in paragraph 3 of EO 9611 that the War Shipping Administration be guided by the Board's determination survived the Board's period concerns EO 9611, not this order, and is not decided here.
